the Frequent Value phenomenon is a useful tool for designing energy efficient data caches.

the frequent value phenomenon can significantly reduce energy consumption of caches.

the design of an efficient and energy efficient cache for a wide class of applications.
the design of an energy efficient cache for the next generation of microprocessors.
the design of energy efficient data cache for embedded systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FVC design provides a good tradeoff between performance and energy efficiency.
the FVC is an effective way to reduce energy consumption in a cache.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 64 Kb FVC can be used in place of a 64 Kb cache to save energy with only a small increase in performance delay.
a 64 Kb FVC can be used to reduce Ll cache energy by 28% with an average increase in execution time by 2.5%.
a 32 Kb/64-value cache would provide 14% reduction in L1 cache energy and 1.69% increase in execution delay.

the Frequent Value data cache design is energy efficient and provides a good trade off between performance and energy efficiency.
